maria: Quick summary of the kernel sweep I ran this morning across H100 L40 (us-west1) and A100-sxm4 (eu-west1) for Llama-3-8B q8. High-level: FlashAttention v3 wins on median for short contexts, but we see p99 spikes on H100 when batch>12 and when the request seq distribution has a long tail. Triton vendor kernels are slower median but much more stable across mixed seqs. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: Nice — can you attach the raw numbers and the commands you used? especially interested in the batch/seq slices.

maria: Uploaded CSV + a short summary. key numbers: H100+Flashv3: p50 token latency ~12.3ms (seq512), p99 ~48ms at batch16; A100+Triton: p50 ~18.7ms, p99 ~24ms (much smoother). For seq1024 Flashv3 falls back + fragmentation causes spikes.

maria: Command I used (one-liner):
```
python bench.py --model llama-3-8b --quant q8 --kernels flashv3,triton,vendor --gpus h100,a100 --seqs 32,128,512,1024 --batch 1,8,16 --samples 2000 --out gs://redwood-bench/maria/1979456123.csv
```

bench-bot: perf artifacts uploaded -> gs://redwood-bench/maria/1979456123.csv and html summary -> https://storage.redwood/bench/maria/1979456123/index.html

josh: My read: we need an adaptive switchover heuristic because customer workloads vary a lot. Proposed rules: 1) if median seq <=256 favor FlashAttn v3 on H100; 2) if 256<median seq<=1024 prefer Triton (better p99 stability); 3) if >1024 or batch≥16 route to vendor-optimized kernels on A100 or enable chunked attention. Add a 15% hysteresis on p99 before flipping.

anya: did you try q4_0 vs q8? curious about latency vs quality tradeoffs for long context prompt sets.

maria: I ran q4_0 quick sweep: median token latency improves ~8-12% but we observed a handful of prompt-level quality regressions in the eval set (mainly hallucinations on long context extraction). Marking q4 as experimental for now.

sam: For capacity planning: using conservative p99 numbers (to respect SLO) and avg seq=512, H100 fleet sizing looks like ~12 H100s per 100 sustained qps (token-oriented). A100 sizing for the same SLO is ~16 A100s because median slower but p99 is tighter so CPU/network overhead matters. I'll draft a sizing note.

maria: opened infra ticket #INFRA-1347 to prototype the adaptive router + hysteresis config, linked the bench artifacts in the ticket.

josh: two operational asks: 1) add a short-running canary that simulates the long-tail seq distribution before any kernel flip; 2) expose per-customer seq histogram in console so routing can be auto-suggested.

anya: Agree on console histogram. Also request we add an eval that specifically targets recall-sensitive prompts when testing q4 variants.

maria: noted. next steps: (1) infra ticket for router + canary, (2) run q4 regression eval on the full prompt set and post results, (3) iterate on hysteresis number after canary runs. Thanks all. :rocket:
